beats.narration_text: Merhaba. This is Liam, in for Bear, with chapter four of INFO 7375, Computational Skepticism for AI, at Northeastern. This film is about one word on a vendor's slide: robust. Robustness is a profile, not a number: one row per attack class, at a stated budget. You'll watch a template table fill: three robust numbers under one word. The trap: letting the word stand in for the table.

props.heading: What This Film Is About
props.question: A vendor says the model is 94% accurate and robust. Robust against what?
lines: Robustness is a profile, not a number: one row per attack class, at a stated budget.
Watch a template disclosure table fill: 94% clean in every row; robust 71, 58, 87.
The trap: letting one word, or one number, stand in for a table with blanks.

beats.narration_text: Why should you care? Every model card and vendor deck you read says robust, and the word arrives before the evidence does. Take the word, and you inherit whichever attack nobody tested. Ask against what, and a marketing sentence turns into a specification you can check. And it unlocks writing the robustness section of a deployment document yourself, honestly, blanks included.

beats.narration_text: Four words you'll hear. Clean accuracy: the score on untouched test inputs. Perturbation budget, epsilon: how far any one input value may move. Transfer attack: a perturbation built on a stand-in model, aimed at the real one. Distribution shift: the world drifting from the training data, no attacker required.

the most any single input value is allowed to move — no pixel shifts past it

the world drifts away from the training data; no attacker required

learn.question: A slide says 94% accurate and robust. What does the second word measure?
learn.action: Give the number its bar; look for the word's bar.
learn.observation: The number has a height; the word has nothing to point at.
learn.inference: 'Robust' has no referent until an attack and a budget are named.
learn.next_question: What does one named attack do to the 94?

beats.narration_text: One slide. Ninety-four percent accurate, and robust. The ninety-four has a bar; you can see how tall it is. The other word has nothing. Robust — against what? Against a pixel push nobody can see? Against a stranger holding a copy of your training data? Against next quarter? The slide doesn't say. Let's make it say.

shot.visual_intent: The vendor's sentence in serif at centre: '94% accurate, and robust.' A single ink bar grows to 94 beneath the number, labelled 94%; a terracotta dot lands beside the word 'robust'; the question 'robust against what?' writes below.

show.event: the 94 bar grows under the number
terracotta dot beside 'robust' on 'the other word'

shot.motion_claim: The bar is the persistent object (it becomes row one's clean bar); the word has no bar — that gap is the section.

learn.question: What does one named attack, at a named budget, do to the 94?
learn.action: Fill row one: white-box, ε = 0.03; grow the robust bar.
learn.observation: Clean stays 94; robust at this budget is 71.
learn.inference: A robust accuracy is a number in a row: attack class, budget, value.
learn.next_question: Does a different attack class give the same number?

beats.narration_text: Row one. A white-box attack: the attacker holds the weights, and may nudge every pixel by at most epsilon, zero point zero three. The clean bar stays at ninety-four. The robust bar — accuracy on the attacked inputs — lands at seventy-one. Same model, same test set. One row, one attack, one budget, one number.

shot.visual_intent: The sentence shrinks to a dim claim line top-left; the 94 bar slides into row one's clean slot and turns dim; the header and legend land (attack class · budget · clean · robust at budget); row one's labels 'white-box attack' and 'ε = 0.03' write; the robust bar grows to 71 in ink with '71%' and a terracotta dot beside it; the caption 'template values — illustrative' lands bottom-left.

show.event: sentence to the claim line; the bar slides into row one
robust bar grows to 71 on 'lands at seventy-one'

shot.motion_claim: The first instance: the same bar, now in a row with an attack class and a budget; the robust bar grows to its own height.

learn.question: Does a different attack class give the same number?
learn.action: Fill row two: transfer, surrogate model; grow the bars.
learn.observation: Clean 94 again; robust 58 — a different number, though the attacker never touched the model.
learn.inference: Each attack class gets its own robust number; one row does not predict another.
learn.next_question: So can the vendor fold these back into one word?

beats.narration_text: Row two. A transfer attack. The attacker never saw this model. They trained a stand-in on the same data, built the perturbation there, and aimed it here. Clean: still ninety-four. Robust, in this template: fifty-eight. Two rows, two numbers. Nothing in row one told you row two.

shot.visual_intent: Row two's labels 'transfer attack' / 'surrogate model' write; its clean bar grows to 94 (dim) and its robust bar to 58 (ink) with '58%'; the terracotta dot moves to 58; a dim caption bottom-right: 'the attacker never saw the model'.

show.event: clean bar to 94; robust bar to 58 on 'fifty-eight'
caption: the attacker never saw the model

shot.motion_claim: The second parametrized instance: vary the attack class, replay the fill; 58 is not 71.

learn.question: Can two robust numbers be summarized by one word?
learn.action: Merge the two bars into one labelled 'robust'.
learn.observation: The numbers disappear; the word cannot say which row it came from.
learn.inference: The single word is not a summary; it is a deletion.
learn.next_question: What arrangement keeps every number where it belongs?

beats.narration_text: Now the vendor's move. Take those two bars and fold them back into one word. Robust. Watch what happens to the numbers. They're gone. Which one was it — seventy-one? Fifty-eight? The word has no slot for the answer. It sounds like evidence. It is a confident, well-formed word standing in for evidence it does not carry. The fluency trap, in a lab coat.

shot.visual_intent: The two robust bars and their labels slide together and merge into one ink bar between the rows, labelled with the single word 'robust' (no number); a terracotta X lands beside the word; caption bottom-right: 'the fluency trap in a lab coat'.

show.event: the two robust bars slide together and merge on 'fold them back'
X beside 'robust' on 'no slot for the answer'

shot.motion_claim: The natural wrong turn walked to its limit: the merge is lossy on screen — two numbers become none.

learn.question: What arrangement keeps every number where it belongs?
learn.action: Unfold the merged bar back into rows; add a row with no attacker.
learn.observation: Each row carries its class, its budget and its number; row three is open.
learn.inference: Robustness is a profile — one axis per row — not a score.
learn.next_question: With no attacker at all, where does row three land?

beats.narration_text: Here's the reframe. Unfold it. Each row is its own axis. A number lives in its row, with its attack class and its budget, and never leaves it. That is the representation: not a score, a profile. Now a third row, and this one has no attacker at all. Natural drift: the same model, inputs from a later time window. Clean, ninety-four again. Robust — blank.

shot.visual_intent: The merged bar splits back into 71 and 58 in their rows (the reverse morph); row three's labels 'natural shift' / 'time shift only' write; its clean bar grows to 94 (dim); its robust slot shows a dim '?'; caption bottom-right: 'no attacker; the world moved'.

show.event: the merged bar splits back into rows one and two
'a profile' — the rows read as separate axes
row three: labels, clean bar to 94

shot.motion_claim: The representation arrives: rows as separate axes; the third row's robust value is deliberately withheld for the predict beat.

learn.question: Where does the no-attacker row land relative to 58 and 71?
learn.action: Draw the guides; hold the picture.
learn.observation: The viewer commits to a band.
learn.inference: A prediction makes the reveal evidence about whether rows predict each other.

beats.narration_text: Before it lands — commit. The insider got the model down to seventy-one. The stranger, fifty-eight. Now nobody attacks; the world just moves. Where does row three land? Above seventy-one? Between? Below fifty-eight? And the harder question: could the two attack rows have told you?

shot.visual_intent: Two dim tick marks land on row three's scale at 58 and 71 (the guides); a terracotta dot sits beside the '?'; the question 'above 71, between, or below 58?' writes lower-left; everything else holds still.

show.event: guide ticks at 58 and 71 on row three

shot.motion_claim: The predict-before-reveal beat: guides drawn, value withheld.

learn.question: Where does row three land, and what else does the form ask?
learn.action: Land 87; hand the sentence the residual-risk and monitoring fields.
learn.observation: 87 sits above both attack rows; the two fields stay blank.
learn.inference: The rows do not predict each other, and a word cannot fill a field.
learn.next_question: Is a robust number at least fixed once measured?

beats.narration_text: Eighty-seven, in this template. Above both. And no, the attack rows could not have told you: surviving an attacker does not guarantee surviving time, or the reverse. Now hand the slide the rest of the form. What was not tested? Blank. What will you watch in production, and when do you pull it? Blank. The word has nothing to write here.

shot.visual_intent: Row three's robust bar grows to 87 with '87%' — past both guide ticks; then the collision: the dim claim line's word 'robust' slides down and transforms into two ghost blank fields beneath the table — 'residual risk' and 'monitoring trigger' — which stay empty; a terracotta dot beside 87%.

show.event: the bar grows to 87, past both ticks
the claim's 'robust' morphs into two blank fields on 'the rest of the form'

shot.motion_claim: The aha is the morph: the reveal breaks the one-number reading, and the word meets the form and fills nothing.

learn.question: Is a robust number fixed once measured?
learn.action: Double row one's budget and watch its number.
learn.observation: The number cannot travel with the row; at a new budget it is unknown.
learn.inference: A robust accuracy is a value AT a budget; the budget is part of the number.
learn.next_question: Say the whole structure as a rule.

beats.narration_text: One more thing, and it's the part people skip. Change one thing in row one: the budget. Same attack, double the push. Is it still seventy-one? Nobody knows. That number was measured at zero point zero three, and it stays there. A robust accuracy is a number at a budget. Move the budget, and you owe a new measurement.

shot.visual_intent: Row one's budget label morphs 'ε = 0.03' → 'ε = 0.06'; its robust bar drains to a ghost bar and '71%' becomes '?'; a terracotta dot beside the new budget; then the budget morphs back to 0.03 and the bar refills to 71; caption bottom-right: 'a number at a budget'.

show.event: budget label → ε = 0.06 on 'double the push'
budget back to 0.03; bar refills to 71

shot.motion_claim: Post-shift instance: hold everything, vary the budget — the number is bound to it (no invented value is shown).

learn.question: What is the rule?
learn.action: Label the three sections of the disclosure and join them with one rail.
learn.observation: Profile, residual risk, monitoring trigger — the form has a shape.
learn.inference: A robustness claim is this structure or it is not a claim.

beats.narration_text: This deserves its name. Robustness is a profile, not a number. Section one: for each attack class, the budget, the clean accuracy, and the robust accuracy at that budget. Section two: the residual risk — what was not tested, in writing. Section three: the monitoring trigger — what you watch, and when a human steps in. A claim without this structure is not a claim.

shot.visual_intent: The form gets its section labels: 'Section 1 · profile' over the table, 'Section 2 · residual risk' and 'Section 3 · monitoring trigger' beside the blanks; a bracket-free ink rail draws down the left edge joining the three sections; 'a profile, not a number' lands bold at right; caption: 'no structure, no claim'.

show.event: sections 2 and 3 labelled beside the blanks; the rail draws

shot.motion_claim: The abstraction arrives as the name for the form the viewer watched fill: three sections, one structure.

learn.question: So — what does the slide's word measure?
learn.action: Point the word at the rows, one by one.
learn.observation: Three numbers, three rows, two blanks — and the 94 never moved.
learn.inference: 'Robust against what' has an answer only as a profile.

beats.narration_text: Back to the slide. Ninety-four percent: that's the clean column, the one that never moved. Robust — against what? Now you can point. A white-box push at zero point zero three: seventy-one. A transfer attack: fifty-eight. A time shift: eighty-seven. And two blanks nobody filled. Not taught here: what each defense buys and what it costs. That's the next reading.

shot.visual_intent: The dim claim line returns to a full-size sentence at the right; a terracotta dot travels from its '94%' down the clean column, then from its 'robust' down the robust column 71 → 58 → 87, then to the two blanks; an X lands beside 'robust'; boundary caption: 'not taught: what each defense costs'.

show.event: dot from '94%' to the clean column on 'never moved'
dot walks the robust column 71 → 58 → 87 on the spoken numbers
dot to the blanks; X beside 'robust'

shot.motion_claim: The HOOK's sentence and bar resolve against the filled form; the boundary is one dim line.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Robust is not a number; it is a profile — one row per attack class, at a stated budget, clean and robust accuracy side by side. The rows are separate axes: seventy-one, fifty-eight and eighty-seven do not predict each other. Move the budget and the number expires. And the form has two more sections, residual risk and a monitoring trigger, that a single word never fills. A claim without this structure is not a claim.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: You are reviewing a facial-recognition system proposed for a physical access-control door. The vendor claims the model is 'robust against adversarial examples.' Write five specific questions that would turn that claim into a usable specification, and for each question say what it tests. At least one question must ask for an attack class and a perturbation budget; at least one must ask what was NOT tested; and at least one must ask what will be monitored in production and what triggers a human review. Two things to look for. Does every question name something measurable — an attack class, a budget, a number — rather than asking how robust it is, again? And did it leave room for the blanks: what was not tested, and what gets watched.
